package_info.why_malicious: This version of the package is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution (RCE) due to the unsafe behavior of the InvokerTransformer class. When deserializing attacker-controlled data, InvokerTransformer can invoke arbitrary methods via reflection, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code on the host system. This critical vulnerability enables full compromise of applications that deserialize untrusted input, making this package version highly dangerous for production use.

execution_context.trigger: Deserialization of attacker-controlled data at runtime

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Enables invocation of arbitrary methods on attacker-controlled objects during deserialization, which can be exploited to achieve remote code execution via reflection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The transform method uses reflection to invoke any method specified by the serialized payload, without validating the method or input. When deserialization occurs on untrusted data, an attacker can craft a payload that causes execution of arbitrary code, such as spawning a shell or downloading malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal deserialization should not result in execution of arbitrary code or methods controlled by external input. This code violates the expectation that deserialization is a passive process and does not allow attackers to control method invocation or execute system commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Reflection is legitimately used for dynamic method invocation in frameworks and libraries, but secure implementations restrict which methods can be called and do not allow untrusted input to control method names or arguments. In this case, the lack of such restrictions enables exploitation.
key_indicators: Use of java.lang.reflect.Method.invoke() on attacker-supplied objects
No validation or restriction on method or arguments during deserialization
Presence of InvokerTransformer in deserialization call chain
Ability to trigger system-level commands (e.g., Runtime.getRuntime().exec()) via crafted payloads

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a serialized object containing a malicious InvokerTransformer payload that specifies a method and arguments to invoke.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deserialization of the object by a vulnerable application

attack_chain.action: Application deserializes the attacker-supplied object, triggering the InvokerTransformer's transform method.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary method invocation via reflection, as specified by the attacker

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is executed on the server, such as executing system commands or opening a reverse shell, resulting in remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the application or server, allowing attacker control

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of untrusted data containing InvokerTransformer objects
Reflection-based method invocation (java.lang.reflect.Method.invoke) during or immediately after deserialization
Unexpected execution of system-level commands (e.g., Runtime.getRuntime().exec()) in deserialization code paths
Presence of InvokerTransformer in object graphs being deserialized
file_indicators: Use of commons-collections:3.2.1 in dependency manifests (pom.xml, build.gradle, ivy.xml)
References to InvokerTransformer in application source code or serialized data
network_indicators: Outbound network connections initiated by the application process immediately following deserialization (e.g., reverse shell, download of secondary payloads)
Unusual external connections from the application server that coincide with deserialization events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan dependency manifests for vulnerable versions of commons-collections (<=3.2.1). Use static analysis to identify code paths that deserialize untrusted input and reference InvokerTransformer. Monitor application logs and runtime behavior for reflection-based method invocations and unexpected calls to Runtime.getRuntime().exec() or similar APIs during or after deserialization. Employ runtime instrumentation or security agents to detect deserialization of objects containing InvokerTransformer and block or alert on such events. Correlate outbound network activity with deserialization events to identify potential exploitation.
